nodes.label: Data Folder Configuration (config.json)
nodes.rationale: Folder locations live in config.json next to app.py and are resolved relative to app.py's own location (not the working directory) unless absolute. Env vars MAQAM_RESULTS_DIR / MAQAM_AUDIO_ROOT / MAQAM_REF_DIR override both the config file and the Settings panel, so per-run overrides need no file edits.

nodes.label: Per-take Identity
nodes.rationale: A bare filename is not unique: the same generated track can exist in several run folders, each a different audio file ranked independently. The app therefore keys ratings, stats, and playback by the composite '<run folder>/<filename>' from the CSV 'file' column, so ratings stay independent across takes and shared between full and top-N views.

nodes.label: Ratings Storage
nodes.rationale: Stored as plain JSON, one file per category at results_dir/ratings/<category>.json, keyed by per-take identity rather than rank or bare filename. On load, basename-keyed legacy ratings are migrated; ambiguous basenames mapping to multiple takes are left inactive rather than guessing.

nodes.label: Compare Panel (Reference vs. Under Study)
nodes.rationale: Signature element: side-by-side reference and candidate players with score badge and inline star rating directly under the candidate player, keeping rating at the same toolbar weight as playback.

nodes.label: Catalog Stats Dashboard (Proposed Home Page)
nodes.rationale: Proposed front (home) page: replaces the plain 'Select a Maqam' empty state with per-maqam listening stats (candidates, rated, completion %, avg rating, star histogram). The Filter & Sort panel is intentionally excluded because it only appears once a maqam is open.

nodes.label: Reference vs. Candidate Listening & Rating Tool
nodes.norm_label: reference vs. candidate listening & rating tool
nodes.rationale: Built as a small local Flask app for A/B listening; ranking is driven entirely by user-supplied CSVs, so the app has no opinion about the domain. Originally for acoustic-similarity review but deliberately domain-agnostic: anything expressible as 'one reference item, many candidates, a numeric score' fits.
